body:
> **Now primarily tracked in-repo at `workshop/issues/000003-per-state-source-registry.md`** — this issue remains as a public-visibility stub per the ariadne in-repo-first convention. The original spec is preserved below.

---

## Goal

As coverage expands beyond California, each state needs its own `sources/<state>.md` listing authoritative outlets (Tier A primary, Tier B authoritative-secondary) for that jurisdiction. The tier-classification principle lives in `calibration-skills/source-hygiene-tier-list.md`; the concrete per-state outlet registries are what unblocks accurate research in new states.

## Current state

- `sources/US.md` — federal (FEC, Congress.gov, AP, Reuters, NPR, Politico, etc.)
- `sources/CA.md` — California (CalMatters, KQED, LA Times, SF Chronicle, EdSource, regional broadsheets, county registrar voter-info tools for SM/LA/SF/SAC/SC/AC/SD/OC)

## Phased expansion

Track per-state in the existing scaling issue (#1). Each Phase-1 / Phase-2 state addition should be accompanied by `sources/<state>.md` populated *before* the candidate-research run, so the research subagents have the right outlet list from the start.

Concretely:
- Add a state to the coverage plan → seed `sources/<state>.md` with its key outlets first
- Then run `scripts/populate-jurisdiction.sh STATE=<X> YEAR=<Y>` using those sources
- Refine `sources/<X>.md` based on what the research surfaces (outlets discovered during research get tier-classified and added back)

## What sources to include per state

For each state, capture:

**Tier A — Primary / official**
- State Secretary of State elections office
- State legislature voting/bill records
- State campaign-finance filing system (per-state equivalent of FPPC)
- County registrar voter-info tools (top ~10 counties by population first)

**Tier B — Authoritative-secondary**
- Statewide nonpartisan policy outlets (e.g., CalMatters equivalent — Texas Tribune, NJ Spotlight, etc.)
- Statewide public-radio voter guide if it exists
- One or two mainstream state-of-record newspapers
- Specialized outlets if dominant in the state (e.g., EdSource for CA education)

**Tier B-local — Regional broadsheets**
- One per major metro area in the state

**Tier C — Use with caution**
- Wikipedia (orientation only)
- Known partisan local outlets (tilt-flagged)

## PR policy

Unlike candidate research / controversies / ballot manifests (which are factual substrate and not accepted as PRs to avoid the Wikipedia bias dynamic), `sources/` PRs are **welcomed**. Sources are research methodology metadata — disagreement about which outlets are authoritative is itself useful signal and surfaces faster via PR review.

PR acceptance criteria:
- Tier classification follows the rule in `calibration-skills/source-hygiene-tier-list.md`
- Each outlet entry has a brief context line (region, tilt if any, specialty)
- Tier C entries explicitly flag tilt

## Initial targets after CA

Following the scaling roadmap in #1:
- US-major-coverage states first: TX, NY, FL (Phase 1 battle-test)
- Then: PA, IL, OH, GA, NC, MI (large electoral states)
- Then: rest of US per Phase 2
title: Build out per-state authoritative-source registry (sources/ directory)
